Prior to joining Booth, Almagro was a Junior Scholar of the Opportunity and Inclusive Growth Institute at the Minneapolis Fed.

Almagro holds a PhD in economics from New York University. Additionally, she earned an MSc in econometrics & mathematical economics from London School of Economics, a BA in Economics from University of Cambridge, and a Licentiate degree in Mathematics from Universidad Complutense de Madrid.

7892.name: Christine  Carpenter
7892.title: Clinical Professor of Leadership
7892.bio:
Dr. Christine Carpenter is a Clinical Professor of Leadership at the University of Chicago Booth School of Business and a licensed clinical psychologist with over two decades of experience in private practice. Her work focuses on the conscious and unconscious dynamics that shape interpersonal behavior, with particular expertise in group process and relational development.

Dr. Carpenter has led long-standing interpersonal process groups and has facilitated numerous training groups through the Great Lakes Group Psychotherapy Society, where she currently serves as president. Her enduring belief in the power of group work to catalyze personal and professional growth informs both her clinical and academic practice.

In 2013, Dr. Carpenter founded Evolve Dating, a coaching practice supporting high-achieving individuals who seek more meaningful and connected romantic partnerships. Her work in this space bridges psychological insight with practical relational strategy.

At Booth, she has been involved in the course Interpersonal Dyanamics since it's inception at Booth in 2019 when she started as a cofacilitator/coach in one of the two innaugural sections. She now teaches 6 of the more than 25 sections offered per year. The rapid growth and popularity of the course among students reflects the value of programs that develop emotional intelligence, self-awareness and effective communication skills - including giving and receiving feedback in a way that keeps defenses low. 

Dr. Carpenter is also a founding partner of DeepNorth, a leadership coaching practice that brings psychologically grounded, experiential development work to executives and senior teams. At the core of her work—whether in therapy, teaching, or coaching—is a deep commitment to helping individuals lead from within, with presence, clarity, and purpose.

7901.name: Lara  Kattan
7901.title: Clinical Assistant Professor of Operations Management
7901.bio:
Lara is a data scientist and machine learning engineer with particular interests in financial modeling and Bayesian financial statistics. At Booth, she teaches Python, SQL, and R courses.

She has previously been a consultant at McKinsey and EY, specializing in machine learning for finance. Kattan holds an MPP in public policy (econometrics concentration) from the University of Chicago, and a BA in economics and political science from Northwestern University.

7940.name: Anders  Humlum
7940.title: Associate Professor of Economics
7940.bio:
Anders Humlum is an economist studying how automation and AI affect workers and firms. His research spans modern technologies, such as AI chatbots and industrial robots, and historical innovations, such as steam engines during the Industrial Revolution. He collects micro-level data on how new technologies are adopted and traces their effects on employment, wages, firm survival, and profitability. His work also sheds light on how reskilling policies can help workers adapt to disruptions in the labor market.

Humlum holds a Ph.D. in Economics from Princeton University and a B.Sc. in Economics from the University of Copenhagen. Prior to joining Booth in 2022, he was a postdoctoral research fellow at the Becker Friedman Institute.

7942.name: Tom  Hafen
7942.title: Adjunct Professor of Marketing
7942.bio: Tom Hafen is currently Vice President of Marketing Communications at Goldman Sachs where he leads consumer communications on Marcus by Goldman Sachs. Prior to Goldman Sachs, Hafen was Head of Marketing on National Growth Brands at Nestle Waters USA. Hafen's past roles include leading marketing for the Gerber Infant Formula Business at Nestle, managing the Iams pet care brand at Procter and Gamble, and leading U.S. marketing for tablets and phones at Microsoft. He also helped lead the Winnie the Pooh brand at the Walt Disney Corporation. He has been a Lecturer in Management at Yale University School of Management and an Adjunct Professor of Marketing at Columbia Business School. His publications include research on digital marketing, social media, and U.S. business history. Hafen holds an MBA and PhD from the University of Chicago.

7963.name: Britt  Raphling
7963.title: Clinical Professor of Leadership
7963.bio: Britt Raphling is Clinical Professor of Leadership at the University of Chicago’s Booth School of Business, where she has co-facilitated and taught Interpersonal Dynamics since Spring 2020.  She is a Licensed Clinical Professional Counselor (LCPC) and a Certified Group Psychotherapist (CGP) with a private psychotherapy practice in Chicago.  She has a Master’s degree in Counseling Psychology from Northwestern University (2006) and is a graduate of the Center for Group Studies’ training program in Modern Analytic group psychotherapy (2018).  Britt has been an Institute Leader for the American Group Psychotherapy Association (AGPA).  She has presented numerous experiential trainings in group therapy locally and nationally, for the Great Lakes Group Psychotherapy Society (GLGPS) and AGPA. Her chapter, "A Very Civilized Tea Party:  A Leader's Resistance to Aggression in a Women's Group, is published in the 2021 book, Women, Intersectionality and Power in Group Psychotherapy Leadership.

8555.name: Anna  Costello
8555.title: Jeffrey Breakenridge Keller Professor of Accounting and Applied AI, and John E. Jeuck Faculty Fellow
8555.bio:
Anna Costello is Professor of Accounting. Before joining Booth, she previously served as an Assistant Professor of Accounting at University of Michigan Ross School of Business and MIT Sloan School of Management. Costello received her Bachelors and Masters of Business Administration from the University of Notre Dame and a PhD in Business Administration from the University of Chicago. Prior to earning her graduate degrees, Anna worked as a senior auditor for Deloitte.

Costello's research investigates the role of information sharing between supply chain partners. Specifically, her work shows that information asymmetry between buyers and suppliers impacts the terms and restrictions in long-term supply contracts. She also studies how trade credit between supply chain partners influences firm-specific and market-wide risk. Her research has been published in the Journal of Political Economy, the Journal of Financial Economics, the Journal of Accounting Research, the Journal of Accounting and Economics, and The Accounting Review. Costello was awarded the Best Dissertation Award from the Financial Accounting and Reporting Section of the American Accounting Association. She received the 2014-2015 MBA Teacher of the Year Award from the MIT Sloan School of Management.

8557.name: Ghian  Foreman
8557.title: Adjunct Assistant Professor of Strategy
8557.bio:
Ghian Foreman is the president and CEO of the Emerald South Economic Development Collaborative, which generates community wealth and amplifies local culture through shared pride, power, and investment for Chicago’s mid-South Side. Emerald South attracts and coordinates investment through community convening and collaborative partnerships that increase local ownership and prosperity. 

Prior to joining Emerald South, Foreman was the executive director of the Greater Southwest Development Corporation, a community development corporation focused on the improvement of the Southwest Side of Chicago. 

Foreman is the managing partner of the Washington Park Development Group, a real estate development firm focused on traditionally underserved urban markets. In this capacity, he has been responsible for over $50 million in investments and development. Foreman sits on several boards, including the Chicago Rehab Network, Chicago Housing Authority Support Corporation. He is currently the President of the Chicago Police Board, and most recently joined Chicago Booth as Adjunct Assistant Professor of Strategy.

He earned a BS from Florida A&M University and an MBA from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business. A native Chicagoan, he lives in Kenwood with his wife, Traci, and daughter, Jade.

8562.name: Christopher  Campos
8562.title: Associate Professor of Economics and Centel Foundation/Robert P. Reuss Faculty Scholar
8562.bio:
Christopher Campos is a labor economist whose research focuses on the economics of education. Before pursuing higher education, he served in the United States Marine Corps and served tours in Iraq and Southeast Asia.

Campos received a PhD in Economics from UC Berkeley.  Additionally, he earned a BS in Statistics, and a BA in Economics from the University of California, San Diego.

Campos joined Booth in 2022 after spending one year as an Industrial Relations Section Fellow at Princeton University.

8618.name: Will  Gossin
8618.title: Adjunct Assistant Professor of Entrepreneurship
8618.bio:
Will Gossin teaches entrepreneurship and innovation across several professional schools at the University of Chicago including Chicago Booth. He teaches experiential courses on innovation, human-centered design, new venture creation, and social entrepreneurship at the Harris School of Public Policy; the Crown Family School of Social Work, Policy, and Practice; and the Law School. Additionally, he directs the leadership program at the Harris School of Public Policy and is an advisor to startups and government leaders.

Previously, he led Chicago Booth’s social entrepreneurship and impact investing programs, coached over 140 teams in Polsky Center new venture accelerator programs, and taught in the Booth Executive Education program in Hong Kong, New Delhi, and London. He was Assistant Dean in the Social Sciences Division where he was responsible for the career services and equity recruitment and admissions for 12 graduate programs as well as created an urban innovation program. Before working at UChicago, he cofounded a funded social venture and conducted education research and policy analysis at the American Institutes for Research. 

He holds Masters degrees in Social Science Research and Epistemology (UChicago), Mental Health Counseling (Univ of Cincinnati), and a Bachelors degree is Economics and Pre-Med from Wake Forest University.

8675.name: Ningzi  Li
8675.title: Adjunct Assistant Professor of Organizations and Strategy
8675.bio:
Ningzi Li is a professional research specialist at the Data Science Insitute (DSI) and adjunct assistant professor at the Booth School of Business at the University of Chicago. She studies cognition of decision-makers in the formation and consequences of organizational strategies, aiming to advance managerial cognition, stakeholder theory, and behavioral theory of the firm.

On one front, she studies financial and non-financial disclosures, such as earnings calls and sustainability reports, asking how distinct communication content or style shape stakeholder perceptions under different market conditions. On another front, she studies patents filed by firms, questioning how managers choose to take risks in knowledge generation. Throughout her projects, she uses natural experiments and various language models to gather rich empirical evidence.

Li earned a doctoral degree in sociology from Cornell University and received B.A. in sociology and economics from Tsinghua University. Prior to joining UofC, she taught at the Leeds School of Business at the University of Colorado Boulder.

8731.name: Kristin  Donnelly
8731.title: Associate Professor of Marketing
8731.bio:
Kristin Donnelly studies a range of topics related to how people make everyday decisions. Among other things, her research asks how people think about time, form preferences, and make inferences based on limited information. Donnelly's research has appeared in a variety of journals, including the Journal of Marketing Research, Psychological Science, Journal of Experimental Psychology: Applied, and Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, and has been featured in Forbes, The Atlantic, Time, Huffington Post, Wall Street Journal and other outlets. Donnelly received the Einhorn Award for her work on time perception. In 2026, she was named a Top 40 Under 40 MBA Professor by Poets & Quants.

Donnelly holds a Ph.D. in Marketing from the Haas School of Business, University of California, Berkeley, an M.A. in Psychology from San Diego State University, and a B.A. in Psychology from the University of Arizona.

8732.name: Chris  Wheat
8732.title: Adjunct Associate Professor of Strategy
8732.bio:
Chris Wheat has more than a decade of experience in environmental policy and politics.  Chris is the Managing Director for Policy and Government Affairs at the Sustainable Cities Fund and Sustainable Cities Action Fund. The Funds provide financial support, technical assistance, and strategic guidance for place-based programs that expand economic opportunity, improve quality of life, and combat the climate crisis. Operating as a strategic regrantor, the Funds partner directly with cities, local organizations, and other subnational actors to help funder initiatives achieve greater impact.

Chris joined the Fund from the Stigler Center for the Study of the Economy and the State at Chicago Booth, where he served as Executive Director. Previously, Chris directed strategy and city engagement for the American Cities Climate Challenge at the Natural Resources Defense Council. Chris also spent seven years in various roles in the Office of Chicago Mayor Rahm Emanuel, including Chief of Policy and Chief Sustainability Officer. Chris is on the Board of Directors at the Center for Neighborhood Technology and the National Advisory Council of the Gephardt Institute for Civic and Community Engagement.

A native of Little Rock, Arkansas, Chris holds a BA from Washington University in St. Louis and an MBA from Chicago Booth.

8774.name: Stephanie  Smith
8774.title: Assistant Professor of Marketing
8774.bio:
Stephanie Smith studies the (in)consistencies of the decision-making process across different domains and decision targets (i.e. self vs. other). In her research, she uses eye tracking and computational modeling to better understand the decision process.

Smith earned a PhD in Decision Psychology from The Ohio State University, and holds a BA from St. Olaf College.

Prior to joining Booth in 2022, Smith was a postdoctoral scholar in Behavioral Decision Making at the UCLA Anderson School of Management. 

Outside of academia and research, Smith loves to run/bike/hike/swim (not all at once) and is an avid traveler: 40+ U.S. states, 30+ countries (so far).

9904.name: Hugh  Cole
9904.title: Adjunct Assistant Professor of Leadership
9904.bio:
Hugh Cole teaches Interpersonal Dynamics in Leadership at Booth.  He is a Licensed Clinical Social Worker, Certified Group Psychotherapist and Certified Alcohol and Drug Counselor from Chicago Illinois. Outside of Booth, Cole is founding partner and COO of Chicago Pride Center, LLC and co-facilitator of Interpersonal Dynamics T-group with Leaders in Tech in California (LIT).

Cole is an Albert Schweitzer Fellow for Life, addressing healthcare disparities at home and abroad, and was the 2012 recipient of Loyola University Chicago President’s Medallion for community service for his group work in the Chicago LGBTQIA+ communities utilizing phenomenological group process. His therapeutic work is informed by his experience of the trauma consultation group at Womencare Counseling in Evanston. Cole served as senior clinician at Howard Brown Health Center where he facilitated group, individual and relational psychotherapy, also providing clinical supervision and consultation addressing issues related to interpersonal effectiveness, identity, grief, substance use, healing from trauma and issues related to the experience of belonging.

Cole received his Master of Social Work from Loyola University Chicago with a mental health concentration. A lifelong learner, he is currently pursuing certifications in Eye Movement Desensitization and Reprocessing (EMDR), The Neuro-Affective Relational Model (NARM) of trauma therapy and Applied Jungian Depth Psychotherapy. He comes from a large and ever-growing family from the South side of Chicago, and his personal passions include family, art, travel, music, theatre, gardening and social justice.

9944.name: Andreas  Kraft
9944.title: Assistant Professor of Marketing, Asness Junior Faculty Fellow and Charles E. Merrill Faculty Scholar
9944.bio:
Andreas Kraft is interested in the consequences of economic frictions (e.g., bounded rationality or informational) across various settings and their effect on marketing actions. His research combines analytical economic models with various empirical tools.

Kraft is originally from Vienna, Austria, and came to the U.S. on a full scholarship to play wheelchair basketball at the University of Texas in Arlington. Kraft was awarded the Fred Moore Assistant Instructor Award for Teaching Excellence (2022) (awarded to the top 2 assistant instructors each year in the business school).

Kraft received a PhD in quantitative marketing from the University of Texas at Austin. Additionally, he earned a BBA in finance and MA in economics at the University of Texas at Arlington.

9950.name: Venkat  Atluri
9950.title: Adjunct Associate Professor of Strategy
9950.bio:
Venkat Atluri is a senior partner with McKinsey & Company, where he leads the firm’s global Tech and Telecommunications practice. He partners with top executives, boards and investors to create value through end-to-end performance transformation, programmatic mergers and acquisitions (M&A), and new business building from scale-up to initial public offerings (IPO). Keenly interested in the future of technology, Venkat brings a special focus on the cross-sector opportunities at the intersection of new technologies and emerging business models. He serves clients in the high-tech, media and telecommunications, advanced industries, and consumer sectors across multiple continents. He also advises venture capital and private equity investors.

Venkat is a leading expert on the vast and emerging opportunities—created by the network connectivity of devices, systems, platforms, and people—powered by software and hardware. He draws on this expertise to guide clients through the design and deployment of network and ecosystem-based businesses across sectors. A thought leader at McKinsey, Venkat is a prolific author and sought-after speaker at industry events.

He has held many leadership positions throughout his tenure at the firm. He currently leads global tech/telecom practice. Venkat cofounded and led McKinsey’s work in Internet of Things (IoT). As the founding member of our New Ventures group, he helped to incubate new analytic and digital assets, develop innovative client offerings, and build alliances and partnerships with innovators. He previously led McKinsey’s Technology, Media, & Telecommunications (TMT) Practice in the Midwest United States. Recently, he spearheaded digital, analytics, and tech-enabled transformations for clients in advanced industries. Venkat also lead efforts globally for the TMT Practice to help clients fast-track and sustain transformational impact through leadership alignment, execution support, capability building, and leadership development; with a distinctive set of assets and exceptional digital-learning programs.

Prior to joining McKinsey, Venkat held global operating (P&L) leadership roles; overseeing large businesses and functions at General Electric as well as product development, management, and deployment at 3M.

Venkat Atluri earned master’s degree in business administration from Booth School of Business from University of Chicago in 2001. 

Venkat Atluri was recognized as The Top 25 Technology Leaders in Consulting for 2022 by The Consulting Report.

Outside of McKinsey, Venkat serves on the board of 1871 - a leading start-up incubator in the world - and Founding member and Chairman of the board for CurrentWater, a nonprofit with a mission to nurture companies that are developing innovative water technologies to solve the world’s water challenges.

9963.name: Anthony  Welsch
9963.title: Assistant Professor of Accounting and Kathryn and Grant Swick Faculty Scholar
9963.bio:
Anthony Welsch's research interests are in corporate taxation, multistate taxation, and tax administration using archival, field experimentation, and survey methods.  He aims to produce research with practical insights that can assist policymakers, governmental agencies, managers, and other researchers. Welsch’s current research primarily focuses on multistate taxation, with an emphasis on examining taxpayer behavior, business investment, and fiscal outcomes. He also has an interest in government accounting and finance.

Prior to pursuing a PhD, Welsch worked professionally as a CPA for six years performing state & local tax compliance and consulting services. 

Welsch received a PhD in Accounting from the University of Texas at Austin.  Additionally, he earned a Master of Accountancy and a B.S. in Business from Miami University in Oxford, Ohio.

9964.name: Bradford  Levy
9964.title: Assistant Professor of Accounting and Applied AI and Asness Junior Faculty Fellow
9964.bio:
Prof. Levy is interested in the intersection between AI, information processing, and financial markets. His research is often interdisciplinary, drawing on his diverse background spanning engineering, economics, and statistics, and has been published in premier venues such as NeurIPS and Management Science. Levy has been quoted and cited by business publications such as the Financial Times, Bloomberg, Wall Street Journal, and Grant’s Interest Rate Observer (March 2021), as well as several centers for thought leadership such as the National Bureau of Economic Research, Harvard Law School, Cooley PubCo, and Law360.

Levy spent nearly a decade in tech and automotive leading analytics, software development, and design teams. During this time, he was granted patents in artificial intelligence and safety technologies. Prior to joining Booth, Levy was a researcher at The Wharton School of the University of Pennsylvania.

Levy received an MA in statistics and a PhD from the University of Pennsylvania, The Wharton School. Additionally, he earned an MBA from the University of Michigan and a BS in mechanical engineering from Worcester Polytechnic Institute.

9980.name: X.Y.  Han
9980.title: Assistant Professor of Operations Management, Applied AI and John E. Jeuck Faculty Fellow
9980.bio:
X.Y.'s research uses large-scale computational experiments and mathematical geometry to deconstruct the operational first principles of modern AI and build productivity-enhancing tools. He co-discovered the now-widely-studied Neural Collapse phenomenon in deep neural network training and co-invented the Survey Descent method for nonsmooth optimization. For these works, he received the ICLR 2022 Outstanding Paper Award and was a finalist for the ICCOPT 2022 Best Paper Prize for Young Researchers. His past and present collaborators include the Frick Art Reference Library in NYC, the Surgical Data Science Collective, and the Veolia North America utilities company.

X.Y. holds a PhD in Operations Research and Information Engineering from Cornell University, an M.S. in Statistics from Stanford University, and a B.S.E. in Operations Research and Financial Engineering from Princeton University.

10027.name: Todd  Connor
10027.title: Adjunct Assistant Professor of Strategy
10027.bio:
Todd Connor is the co-founder of Veterans for All Voters, a national voting rights organization and previously founded Bunker Labs, a national entrepreneurship organization that supports the military community.  He previously founded The Collective Academy, a leadership development organization as well as TASCON Advisors. Connor is currently the William, ’88, and Alison Fitzgerald EIR for Social Entrepreneurship and Nonprofit Board Service at the Rustandy Center. He also serves as lead faculty for the Presidential Leadership Scholars program and the George W. Bush Institute's Veteran Leadership Program, and is the author of Third Shift Entrepreneur (Wiley, 2021).

Connor received an MBA from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business. Additionally, he earned a bachelor's degree in American studies from Northwestern University. He is a U.S. Navy veteran.

10058.name: John  Burrows
10058.title: Senior Lecturer
10058.bio:
John Burrows is a Senior Lecturer at the University of Chicago’s Harris School of Public Policy, where he also serves as the Academic Director for Part-Time Programs and Leadership. At Oxford University’s Saïd Business School, he is an Associate Fellow, teaching MBA and EMBA students each summer. He also teaches the MBA negotiations class at Chicago Booth, a role he held from 2014 to 2018 and resumed in 2023.

In addition to his MBA teaching, John works extensively in executive education, delivering programs on leadership, negotiations, decision-making, strategy, and organizational psychology to senior executives and mid-career professionals. His teaching spans open enrollment programs and custom programs designed for specific organizations, blending his academic expertise with practical applications for diverse industries.

John holds an MBA and PhD in Behavioral Science from Chicago Booth and an MSt in Practical Ethics from Pembroke College, Oxford. His academic interests include the application of AI in teaching and learning, the integration of AI into legal and policy frameworks, and the role of social capital in hybrid and remote-first workplaces.

Before transitioning to academia, John was a partner at Accenture, where he developed extensive expertise in consulting, sales, and marketing. He held senior roles at enterprise software companies such as Siebel and Oracle, and he built European operations while managing an international joint venture in Japan for MarketSwitch, a company later acquired by Experian. Across these roles, he negotiated and led complex, multinational, multimillion-dollar projects spanning business development, international joint ventures, and mergers and acquisitions.

John consults and speaks regularly to organizations across a wide range of industries:

  • Private Sector Clients: Accenture, Alberici, Aon, ARCO Design Build, BNY Mellon, Capgemini, CUES, eBay, Edelman, IWI Wealth Advisors, Kiewit, State Farm, and Women in Leadership Insurance.
  • Healthcare Clients: American College of Surgeons (ACS), American Orthopaedic Association (AOA), Association of Program Directors in Surgery (APDS), BrainLab, CVS Aetna, and Society for Vascular Surgery (SVS).
  • Domestic Public Sector Clients: Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago, State of Wisconsin Investment Board (SWIB), U.S. Army War College, and U.S. Navy.
  • International Public Sector Clients: Saudi Central Bank (SAMA), Decision Support Center (DSC) in the Saudi Royal Court, Saudi Red Sea Authority (SRSA), and the Hong Kong Civil Service Bureau.

John currently serves on the advisory board of Metopio.

10095.name: Jennifer  Fried
10095.title: Adjunct Assistant Professor of Entrepreneurship
10095.bio:
Jennifer Fried is the CEO and Co-Founder of Flow Medical, developer of a next-generation thrombolysis catheter to treat pulmonary embolism. Flow Medical’s technology was invented at the University of Chicago Medical Center by Dr. Jonathan Paul and Dr. Osman Ahmed in 2020. Previously, Fried was the CEO/Co-Founder of Explorer Surgical, also a University of Chicago Medical Center spin-out. She started the company as an MBA student at the University of Chicago Booth School of Business with surgeon researcher Dr. Alex Langerman and led the company from inception to successful exit to GHX in 2021. 

Fried is also active as an investor, serving as a partner for Portfolia’s FemTech Fund as well as a partner at The Fund Midwest, and is an active angel investor and limited partner.  

Previously, Fried was a Vice President at Park Lane Ventures, a healthcare-focused venture capital fund spun out of Essex Woodlands, after beginning her career as a consultant at Bain & Company in Chicago. 

Fried earned a BA with honors from Northwestern University where she studied mathematical methods in the social sciences and economics.  She also holds an MBA with honors from Chicago Booth with concentrations in finance and entrepreneurship.

10108.name: Beidi  Hu
10108.title: Assistant Professor of Marketing and Robert King Steel Faculty Fellow
10108.bio:
Beidi Hu is an Assistant Professor of Marketing at the University of Chicago Booth School of Business. She studies consumer behavior and judgment and decision-making, in particular, how people form and represent beliefs under uncertainty, and how these beliefs shape their judgments and decisions, with applications to consumer choices, forecasting, and managerial decision-making.

She holds a PhD in Decision Processes from the Wharton School, University of Pennsylvania. Additionally, she received a BA summa cum laude in Philosophy, Politics, and Economics from the University of Pennsylvania.

10142.name: Jacob  Conway
10142.title: Assistant Professor of Economics and Fama Faculty Fellow
10142.bio:
Jacob Conway is an Assistant Professor of Economics at the University of Chicago Booth School of Business. His primary research fields are corporate finance and industrial organization. He studies the causes and consequences of firms engaging with social, political, and environmental issues. He also has related research on regulation, polarization, and discrimination.

He holds a PhD in economics from Stanford University. Additionally, he earned bachelor's degrees in mathematics, economics, and statistics from the University of Chicago. Prior to pursuing a PhD, Conway worked as a senior research analyst at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York.

10167.name: Bahar  Taskesen
10167.title: Assistant Professor of Operations Management and Liew Family Junior Faculty Fellow
10167.bio:
Bahar Taskesen’s research interests center around decision-making under uncertainty, large-scale stochastic optimization, and statistical inference. She is particularly interested in exploring algorithmic fairness and robustness and their applications in operations management, control, and machine learning. Her work has implications for the development and deployment of responsible AI systems.

Taskesen earned a PhD from the École polytechnique fédérale de Lausanne (EPFL) in Switzerland, where she was a student in the Risk Analytics and Optimization Lab.  She also holds a BS in electrical and electronics engineering from the Middle East Technical University.

10168.name: Julia  Selgrad
10168.title: Assistant Professor of Finance and Liew Family Junior Faculty Fellow
10168.bio: Julia Selgrad joined Chicago Booth as an Assistant Professor of Finance in 2024. Her research interests include asset pricing, monetary policy, and macro-finance. She graduated with a Ph.D. in Finance from NYU Stern School of Business in 2024. She also earned a B.A. in Economics and Management from the University of Oxford in 2018.

10171.name: Li  Azinovic-Yang
10171.title: Assistant Professor of Accounting and IBM Faculty Fellow
10171.bio:
Li Azinovic-Yang’s research is broadly related to the antecedents and consequences of corporate disclosure. She uses both analytical modeling and data analysis to study the interaction of information disclosure and firm innovation/investment, competition structure and labor practices. 

Azinovic-Yang earned a PhD from Columbia Business School. She also holds a master in banking and finance from the University of Zurich and a bachelor in finance from Shanghai University of Finance and Economics.

10182.name: Anthony  Walker
10182.title: Adjunct Assistant Professor of Entrepreneurship
10182.bio:
Anthony Walker is Founder and General Partner at NCL Partners. NCL participates in the small/medium sized buyout market by making majority and minority investments in later stage companies acquired through the Search model. Anthony has been in the investment management industry for over 20 years.

Prior to founding NCL, Walker was a Vice President in the Global Investment Research Division at Goldman Sachs. While at Goldman, Anthony was responsible for idea generation, client engagement, financial modeling, and marketing the views and opinions of Goldman Sachs related to investments in the Chemicals industry. Prior to Goldman, Walker spent five years managing long/short equities portfolios for Millennium Management and Citadel LLC, trading stocks and managing portfolios across a number subsectors within the Industrial industry.

While at Citadel, he produced the second highest Sharpe Ratio (a measure of risk-adjusted returns) within the firm’s flagship Global Equities business unit. Throughout his career Walker has held several other senior level investment professional positions, including Vice President and Research and Investment Committee Member at Ariel Investments, and Assistant Vice President at Barclays Capital.

Walker received his MBA from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business (Finance and Entrepreneurship) and a BA in Economics and Political Science from Columbia University. He currently a Board of Directors member for eight businesses.

10183.name: Catherine  Littell
10183.title: Adjunct Assistant Professor of Entrepreneurship
10183.bio:
Catherine Littell is an Adjunct Assistant Professor of Entrepreneurship at the University of Chicago Booth School of Business, where she teaches Entrepreneurship Through Acquisition. Her courses draw on both investor and operator perspectives to help students evaluate, acquire, and grow small businesses.

Beyond the classroom, Catherine is the Co-Founder of Legacy 41, an investment firm focused on acquiring and building exceptional lower middle-market companies through a long-term buy-and-build approach. Prior to co-founding Legacy 41, she worked with Halstatt Legacy Partners, the SMB direct investment arm of Halstatt, a multi-generational family office. 

Catherine has spent much of her career in the entrepreneurship through acquisition ecosystem, including a self-funded partnered search and working closely with entrepreneurs and small business owners on financing, growth, and operational scaling. Earlier in her career, she held leadership positions with Redbox Automated Retail and Starwood Hotels & Resorts Worldwide.

Catherine earned her MBA from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business, where she concentrated in entrepreneurship, and holds a BS in Hotel Administration from Cornell University.

10299.name: Anthony  Le
10299.title: Assistant Professor of Accounting and James S. Kemper Faculty Scholar
10299.bio:
Anthony Le’s research interests lie at the intersection of accounting and labor economics. His current research addresses topics such as the impact of accounting regulation and standard setting on the accountant labor market, firms' human capital disclosures,  labor unions' financial reporting mandates, and gender representation in corporate governance.

Le earned a PhD in accounting from Columbia University.  He also holds an MA in economics and a BComm in commerce and economics both from the University of Toronto.

10362.name: Michael  Gray
10362.title: Adjunct Assistant Professor of Entrepreneurship
10362.bio:
Michael Gray is a Partner in the Corporate & Securities practice group at Neal Gerber Eisenberg, where he also leads the firm’s Private Equity, Venture Capital & Growth Companies practice, as well as its Fund Formation & Investment Management practice. He primarily represents private equity sponsors, venture investors, private funds, private equity and venture-backed companies, executives, and family offices.

His extensive experience in complex transactional and corporate governance matters make him an invaluable asset to his clients, who enlist him for advice on mergers and acquisitions, private equity and venture capital investments and portfolio company operations, fund formation, GP stakes and seeding investments, and fund and co-investments.

Gray’s prior experience as an investor facilitating venture capital transactions allowed him to hone his ability to build enduring relationships and connect colleagues to foster business growth.

Gray is currently on the board of the Renaissance Society at the University of Chicago. In addition to teaching at Booth, he is also a frequent guest lecturer at the Kellogg School of Management and the Northwestern Pritzker School of Law and works with the Zell Fellows Program at Kellogg.

Gray holds a J.D. from the Northwestern Pritzker School of Law, an M.S. from the University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign, and a B.A. from the University of Chicago.

10368.name: Brian  Boonstra
10368.title: Adjunct Associate Professor of Finance
10368.bio:
Brian Boonstra is a quantitative researcher based in Chicago.  He has served as senior or chief quant at Jump Trading, Cognitive Capital, UBS O'Connor, Delaware Street Capital, JPMorgan and Helios, and has been teaching at the graduate level since 1996.  He managed Thureos Capital, a hedge fund dedicated to equity/credit arbitrage using contingent claims models, and has worked in most areas of contingent claims modeling and trading.  In addition to teaching at Booth, Boonstra teaches in Financial Mathematics at the University of Chicago.

His interests include numerical analysis, contingent claims pricing models, and statistical learning.  Boonstra holds an S.B. in Mathematics from the University of Chicago and a Ph.D. in Complex Analysis from the University of Michigan.

10466.name: Umang  Khetan
10466.title: Assistant Professor of Finance and Fama Faculty Fellow
10466.bio: Umang Khetan’s research interests include financial intermediation, asset pricing, market structure, and household finance.  Prior to joining Booth, he held roles in fixed income markets at J.P. Morgan Chase and in global equity derivatives at Morgan Stanley. He earned a PhD in Finance from the University of Iowa.

11489.name: Thomas  Wiemann
11489.title: Assistant Professor of Marketing and Beatrice Foods Co. Faculty Scholar
11489.bio:
Thomas Wiemann’s research integrates marketing, econometrics, and machine learning/AI. His current work provides empirical methods for researchers and firms to draw more reliable inferences from data, deepen their understanding of customer demand, and optimize managerial decisions.

Thomas teaches Pricing Strategies in the full-time MBA program. His course equips students with the analytical tools needed to build effective pricing solutions from marketing insights.

Thomas earned a PhD in Economics from the University of Chicago in 2025. He also holds an MSc in Statistical Science from the University of Oxford, and dual BSc degrees in Econometrics & Operations Research and Economics & Business Economics from Erasmus University Rotterdam. During his studies, he gained work experience in Amazon's Consumer Behavior Analytics group.

11501.name: June  Huang
11501.title: Visiting Assistant Professor of Accounting
11501.bio:
June Huang is visiting from the University of Texas at Dallas where she is an assistant professor of accounting. In her research, she studies local government, political economy, and corporate social responsibility (CSR). Before entering academia, she worked in investment banking at J.P. Morgan and CODE Advisors.

Huang holds a PhD in accounting and an MBA from the University of Chicago Booth School of Business, as well as dual BA degrees in Economics and Political Science from the University of Chicago.

11504.name: Sarah  Jabbour
11504.title: Assistant Professor of Applied AI and Fishman Faculty Fellow
11504.bio:
Professor Jabbour studies the design and deployment of AI systems that help humans make decisions in high-stakes environments, with a particular focus on healthcare. Her research is motivated by a central challenge: despite strong performance in controlled settings, AI systems often fail to improve real-world outcomes once deployed. To address this gap, she develops methods for building more reliable AI systems and empirically studies how humans use and are influenced by AI in practice. Her work has been published in top-tier computer science venues, including ECCV and NeurIPS, as well as leading medical and policy journals, including JAMA and Health Affairs.

Prior to joining Booth, Jabbour earned a PhD in Computer Science & Engineering from the University of Michigan. She also completed dual bachelor's degrees in Computer Science & Engineering (BSE) from the University of Michigan College of Engineering and Business Administration (BBA) from the University of Michigan Ross School of Business.

11523.name: Jeremy  Richardson
11523.title: Adjunct Assistant Professor of Behavioral Sciences
11523.bio:
Jerry Richardson studies how emotion and reason shape moral judgment—how we come to see others as good or bad, right or wrong, deserving of praise or blame, and how these judgments differ when applied to ourselves versus others. A parallel line of his research examines reputation management: what people say and do to appear trustworthy and morally good. Across both lines of work, he is driven by questions about how individuals represent other minds, what prompts people to signal (or not signal) their own moral character, and how emotions influence evaluations of other people’s minds and actions. Grounded in real-world phenomena, his research sheds light on the drivers of cooperative, prosocial behavior—and the barriers that block it. 

Richardson earned his PhD in psychology from Cornell University. He also holds an MA in psychology from Cornell University, and a BA in theatre from the University of Maryland.

11536.name: Matteo  Saccarola
11536.title: Adjunct Assistant Professor of Behavioral Sciences
11536.bio:
Matteo Saccarola is a Howard and Nancy Marks Fellow at Booth.  His research interests span behavioral economics, household finance, and real estate, with a particular focus on belief formation and its role in economic decision-making.

He uses large-scale administrative data, applied microeconometric methods, surveys, and online experiments to study how households form, update, and act on beliefs in complex markets and make key life-cycle decisions.

Saccarola holds a PhD in economics from the University of California, Berkeley.  Additionally, he earned an MSc from Bocconi University and a BS in economics from Università Ca’Foscari.

11537.name: John  Stoops
11537.title: Adjunct Associate Professor of Strategic Management
11537.bio: John Stoops brings more than 25 years of experience spanning marketing, entrepreneurship, and higher education. As Vice President-Account Director at Leo Burnett, he led integrated marketing and brand strategy for several Fortune 500 brands including Procter & Gamble and Comcast, directing cross-functional teams and marketing initiatives deployed in more than 160 countries. As Founder and Executive Director of The Revival, he built an arts and education organization from concept to a sustainable enterprise, overseeing strategy, marketing, business development, operations, fundraising, and strategic partnerships while expanding into corporate leadership development and higher education. Stoops serves as an adjunct faculty member at Northwestern University and the University of Chicago, where he teaches strategy, entrepreneurship, leadership, and innovation. He holds a BBA from the University of Wisconsin–Madison and an MBA from Northwestern University's Kellogg School of Management.

11538.name: Jason  Elder
11538.title: Adjunct Assistant Professor of Entrepreneurship
11538.bio:
Jason Elder is a Partner and Managing Director of Corporate Strategy at Performance Trust Capital Partners. He was one of seven original members of the firm and has served on the boards of both Performance Trust Capital Partners, LLC, and Performance Trust Asset Management, LLC. 

Jason is also Chairman of LJE Capital, a family office focused on lower middle market private equity and direct and search-backed acquisitions. 

He is a member of the Entrepreneurship Through Acquisition committee at the Polsky Center for Entrepreneurship and Innovation at his alma mater, the University of Chicago Booth School of Business.  He is also co-founder and board member of Alchemy Analytical Group - the result of a partnered, self-funded search done with a Booth classmate. 

Jason also serves on the board of TimeBank, an Illinois-chartered commercial bank, and on the boards of Northridge Preparatory School and The Willows Academy.

11543.name: Roy  Bahat
11543.title: Adjunct Associate Professor of Entrepreneurship
11543.bio:
Roy Bahat is a Venture Capitalist and the head of Bloomberg Beta, the early-stage venture firm backed by Bloomberg L.P. that invests in startups making work better. Bloomberg Beta treats founders as its customers and was the first venture capital firm to focus on the future of work and the first to focus on artificial intelligence. Bloomberg Beta has invested in Replit, Lambda Labs, MasterClass, Flexport, Campus, and Weights & Biases, among other companies.

Before starting Bloomberg Beta more than a decade ago, Roy started a venture-backed company, was a corporate executive (at News Corp.), in government (at New York's City Hall), in media, and in academia. He was named one of Fast Company’s Most Creative People in Business. Following work he did with New America to understand the long-term effect of technology on work in America, Roy was a commissioner on the California Governor’s Future of Work Commission.

Roy serves on the board or has been an advisor to several non-profits including the Golden Gate Institute for AI, Abundance Network, Stanford's Center on Philanthropy and Civil Society, the Economic Security Project, and the Center for Investigative Reporting. He is a member of Democracy Takes Work, and chairs the Aspen Institute's Business Roundtable on Organized Labor. He proposed the creation of the National Academy for AI Instruction, led by the American Federation of Teachers and United Federation of Teachers. Roy is also a senior fellow (non-resident) at the Brookings Institution, where he writes about AI. Roy hosts a podcast called This Is Not Advice, about how successful people thrive in their occupation (e.g., “how to be a scientist”) and hosts the [Going to Work] conference.

Previously, Roy taught at U.C. Berkeley’s Haas School of Business. He was named one of the favorite MBA professors.

Roy graduated from Harvard College and was a Rhodes Scholar at Oxford University.

11545.name: Laura  Letinsky
11545.title: Professor of Visual Arts
11545.bio:
Laura Letinsky has been a Professor at the University of Chicago in the Visual Arts department since 1994.  She earned a BFA from the University of Manitoba, Winnipeg, Canada, and a MFA in Photography from Yale University’s School of Art. She shows with Yancey Richardson Gallery, NYC, and Document, Chicago and Lisbon, and exhibits internationally including PhotoEspana, Madrid, Museum of Modern Art, NYC, Mumbai Photography Festival, Mumbai, India, MIT, Cambridge, MA, Basel Design, The Photographers Gallery, London, and, Denver Art Museum, CO.

Letinksy’s awards include the Maison Dora Maar Residency, France; Canada Council International Residency, Kunstlerhaus Bethanien Residency, Berlin, The Canada Council Project Grants, The Anonymous Was a Woman Award, and the John Simon Guggenheim Fellowship, and her work is published in monographs and catalogues such as To Want For Nothing, Roman Nvmerals, 2019, Time’s Assignation, Radius Books, 2017, Ill Form and Void Full, Radius Books, 2014, Feast, Smart Museum of Art, UC Press, 2013, After All, Damiani, 2010, Hardly More Than Ever, Renaissance Society, 2004, Blink, Phaidon Press, 2002, and Venus Inferred, University of Chicago Press, 2000.

11552.name: Michele  Gambera
11552.title: Adjunct Professor of Finance
11552.bio:
Michele Gambera, PhD, CFA, is Head of Economic Analysis at Northfield Information Services, a leading risk management analytics provider known for its research-based applications and industry-wide thought leadership. In this role, he draws on decades of experience in institutional portfolio management to develop new features for Northfield’s programs and provide analysis for the firm’s institutional clients.

He joined Northfield in 2026 from UBS Asset Management, where he served as Head of Strategic Asset Allocation and led a team responsible for developing capital market expectations and advising large institutions, including sovereign wealth funds and pension plans, on portfolio diversification and construction. He spent 15 years at UBS.

Earlier in his career, Michele worked at Ibbotson Associates, Morningstar’s asset allocation consultancy, where he served as Senior Research Consultant and Chief Economist beginning in 2006. During more than nine years at Morningstar, he also held roles as Senior Quantitative Analyst and Chief Economist for Morningstar Associates LLC.

Before joining Morningstar, he spent two years as an Economist in the Supervision and Regulation Division of the Federal Reserve Bank of Chicago.

In addition to his extensive experience in economic and quantitative analysis, Michele has a strong academic background. He has published in leading academic journals, including the Journal of Finance, and has held several teaching roles, including at the University of Chicago Booth School of Business and in the Master of Quantitative Finance program at the University of Illinois.

Gambera holds a BA/MA in Economics with honors from the University of Trento in Italy and a PhD in Economics from the Pennsylvania State University. He is a CFA charterholder, co-author of two chapters in the CFA curriculum, as well as a member of the Chicago Quantitative Alliance and the CFA Society of Chicago.

11602.name: Ning  Hao
11602.title: Visiting Professor of Mathematics
11602.bio:
Ning Hao is visiting from the University of Arizona where he is a Professor of Mathematics and a member of the GIDP in Statistics and Data Science. 

He earned a B.S. in Mathematics from Peking University and a Ph.D. in Mathematics from Stony Brook University.

Before joining UA, Hao spent one year as a Research Associate at the statistics lab, Princeton University.

He serves as an Editor for the journal STAT and as an Associate Editor for the Journal of the American Statistical Association and Journal of Computational and Graphical Statistics.

11611.name: Andre  Bauer
11611.title: Visiting Assistant Professor of Econometrics and Statistics
11611.bio:
André Bauer is the founder and elected chair of the SPEC RG Predictive Data Analytics Working Group. Prior to joining Booth, he was an assistant professor in the Department of Computer Science at the Illinois Institute of Technology. 

Bauer believes the overarching goal of his research is to expand the potential of data science to accelerate scientific discovery by integrating advances in data science, artificial intelligence, and systems research. As scientific progress increasingly becomes data-intensive and computationally demanding, unlocking its full potential requires both novel analytical methods and computing infrastructures capable of supporting them efficiently, reliably, and sustainably. His work addresses these challenges through a combination of data science, scientific computing, and performance engineering, leveraging interdisciplinary expertise to develop scalable computational methods and robust software systems that enable emerging data-driven applications across diverse scientific domains. 

Bauer was a postdoctoral researcher at the Department of Computer Science at the University of Chicago and a researcher at Argonne National Laboratory.   He received a PhD in computer science from the University of Würzburg, Germany.
